# Lesson Plan Templates

Ready-to-use templates for different teaching contexts. Copy and fill in.

> For framework guidance (5E, ADDIE, UbD, Hunter), see [frameworks.md](./frameworks.md).  
> For writing learning objectives, see [writing-objectives.md](./writing-objectives.md).

---

## Template A — Traditional Lesson Plan (50–80 min, K-12 or University)

Best for: A single class session using any method. Core structure based on Madeline Hunter + Rosenshine's Principles.

```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
LESSON PLAN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Subject / Course:
Topic:
Grade Level / Audience:
Duration:
Date:
Teacher / Instructor:

───────────────────────────────────────────
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:
1. [Bloom's verb] + [specific content] + [criterion]
2. [Bloom's verb] + [specific content] + [criterion]

───────────────────────────────────────────
STANDARDS / COMPETENCY ALIGNMENT
- [Standard code + description]

───────────────────────────────────────────
PREREQUISITE KNOWLEDGE
Students should already know/be able to:
- 
- 

───────────────────────────────────────────
MATERIALS & RESOURCES
- 
- 

───────────────────────────────────────────
LESSON SEQUENCE

[0:00–0:05] ANTICIPATORY SET / HOOK
Activity:
Key question:
(Purpose: engage attention; surface prior knowledge)

[0:05–0:08] STATE OBJECTIVES & PURPOSE
- "Today we will..."
- "This matters because..."

[0:08–0:18] DIRECT INSTRUCTION / INPUT
- Key concept 1:
- Key concept 2:
- Vocabulary:
- Visual/media used:

[0:18–0:28] MODELING (THINK-ALOUD)
- Worked example 1 (narrate each step):
- Worked example 2:
- Key reasoning to make explicit:

[0:28–0:33] CHECK FOR UNDERSTANDING
Technique: [cold call / mini-whiteboard / poll / TPS]
Question or task:
Success indicator before proceeding:

[0:33–0:55] GUIDED PRACTICE
Activity:
Grouping: [individual / pairs / small group]
Teacher's role during practice:
Common errors to look for:

[0:55–0:68] INDEPENDENT PRACTICE (if time allows)
Task:
Expected success rate:

[0:68–0:75] CLOSURE
Technique: [exit ticket / 3-2-1 / summarize-pair-share]
Prompt:

───────────────────────────────────────────
ASSESSMENT PLAN
- Formative: [what, when, how]
- Summative: [task, due date, format]

───────────────────────────────────────────
DIFFERENTIATION
- Support (struggling learners): [scaffold / tiered task]
- Extension (advanced learners): [enrichment / open-ended task]
- ELL / IEP accommodations: [if applicable]

───────────────────────────────────────────
REFLECTION (complete after lesson)
- What worked?
- What would I change?
- Who was not engaged or is not yet meeting the objective?
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

## Template B — Workshop / Professional Development (2–4 hours)

Best for: Adult learners; professional training; faculty development; team workshops.

```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WORKSHOP PLAN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Workshop Title:
Audience / Participants:
Duration:
Facilitator(s):
Date/Location:

───────────────────────────────────────────
WORKSHOP OBJECTIVES
By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:
1. 
2.
3.

───────────────────────────────────────────
MATERIALS
- Slide deck
- Participant workbook / handout
- Activity materials
- Technology/tools

───────────────────────────────────────────
PRE-WORK (if any)
- Reading:
- Reflection prompt:
- Survey:

───────────────────────────────────────────
WORKSHOP SCHEDULE

[0:00–0:15] WELCOME & CONTEXT SETTING
- Facilitator introduction (brief)
- Agenda and norms
- Icebreaker/energizer:
  Prompt:

[0:15–0:45] THEORY INPUT / FRAMING
- Key concept(s):
- Delivery format: [lecture / video / read-pair-share]
- Discussion question:

[0:45–1:00] ACTIVITY 1 — Application
Format: [individual / pairs / small group]
Task:
Debrief question:

[1:00–1:10] BREAK

[1:10–1:40] ACTIVITY 2 — Analysis / Synthesis
Format:
Task:
Debrief question:

[1:40–2:10] ACTIVITY 3 — Creation / Evaluation
Participants apply learning to their own context:
Task:
Peer feedback protocol: [I Like / I Wonder / What If]

[2:10–2:35] ACTION PLANNING
Prompt: "What will you do differently starting Monday?"
Format: Individual write → share with partner → optional share with room

[2:35–2:50] CLOSURE & QUESTIONS
- Key takeaways recap (facilitator)
- Q&A
- Next steps / resources

[2:50–3:00] EVALUATION
- Post-workshop survey (5 questions max)
- Kirkpatrick Level 1: "Was this valuable? What was most/least useful?"

───────────────────────────────────────────
ASSESSMENT
- Formative: facilitator observation during activities; debrief discussion
- Summative: action plan completion; follow-up check-in (recommend: 2 weeks)

───────────────────────────────────────────
DIFFERENTIATION / ACCESSIBILITY
- Materials available in advance for pre-reading
- Multiple formats for tasks (written / verbal / visual)
- Captions on videos
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

## Template C — Online / Asynchronous Module

Best for: LMS-based e-learning, MOOCs, blended learning, corporate eLearning.

```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ONLINE LESSON PLAN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Course:
Module Number / Title:
Estimated completion time: ___ min
Platform: [Canvas / Moodle / Google Classroom / Articulate / etc.]
Release date:

───────────────────────────────────────────
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of this module, students will be able to:
1. 
2.

───────────────────────────────────────────
MODULE FLOW

[~5 min] 1. ORIENTATION
- Welcome message or brief video (2–3 min)
- Objectives clearly stated
- "Why this matters" — real-world framing

[~15 min] 2. CONTENT DELIVERY
- Video segment 1 (max 6–8 min): [topic]
  → Embedded question: [question at ___ mark]
- Video segment 2 (max 6–8 min): [topic]
  → Embedded question:
- Supplementary reading (optional): [link or attachment]

[~10 min] 3. KNOWLEDGE CHECK
- Auto-graded quiz: 3–5 questions
- Bloom's level targeted: [Remember / Understand]
- Immediate automated feedback enabled: Yes / No
- Attempt limit: [unlimited / 2 attempts]

[~15 min] 4. APPLICATION ACTIVITY
- Task: [apply, analyze, or create]
- Format: [discussion post / short-answer submission / annotated example]
- Submission type: [LMS text box / file upload / peer discussion]

[~5 min] 5. REFLECTION / CLOSURE
- Prompt: "What was the most important idea in this module? What question do you still have?"
- Format: [discussion reply / private journal / ungraded submission]

───────────────────────────────────────────
DISCUSSION FORUM (if applicable)
Initial post prompt:
Reply requirement (e.g., respond to 2 peers):
Grading rubric: [criteria / point value]

───────────────────────────────────────────
ASSESSMENT
- Formative: knowledge check quiz; discussion participation
- Summative: [module assignment or exam; due date]

───────────────────────────────────────────
ACCESSIBILITY & DIFFERENTIATION
- Closed captions on all videos: Yes / No
- Transcript available: Yes / No
- Extended time option for quizzes: Yes / No
- Alternative format available: [audio / text reading]
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

## Template D — Project-Based Learning Unit Plan (Multi-Week)

Best for: PBL units spanning 2–6 weeks. For full PBL methodology, see [../methods/project-based.md](../methods/project-based.md).

```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PBL UNIT PLAN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Unit Title:
Driving Question:
Subject(s):
Grade Level / Audience:
Duration (weeks):
Team Size:

───────────────────────────────────────────
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of this unit, students will be able to:
1. 
2.
3.

───────────────────────────────────────────
PUBLIC PRODUCT
What will students create?
Who is the real audience?
Where / how will it be presented?

───────────────────────────────────────────
STANDARDS ADDRESSED
- 
- 

───────────────────────────────────────────
UNIT OVERVIEW (by week)

WEEK 1 — LAUNCH
- Entry event:
- Introduction to driving question
- "Need to Know" list generation (student-driven)
- Team formation and role assignment

WEEK 2 — INQUIRY & RESEARCH
- Research plan development
- Mini-lesson 1: [topic + method]
- Mini-lesson 2: [topic + method]
- Team research + discussion

WEEK 3 — DEVELOP & CREATE
- Product development begins
- Checkpoint 1: teacher reviews progress
- Mini-lesson 3 (if needed):
- Peer feedback round 1

WEEK 4 — CRITIQUE & REVISE
- External feedback (expert, community, other class)
- Revision based on feedback
- Individual reflection checkpoint

WEEK 5 — FINALIZE & PRESENT
- Final product polish
- Presentation rehearsal
- Public presentation to [audience]
- Individual reflection / debrief

(OPTIONAL) WEEK 6 — EXTENSION / DEEPER INQUIRY

───────────────────────────────────────────
ASSESSMENT PLAN
- Individual content quiz (Week 2): 
- Formative checkpoint (Week 3):
- Peer feedback protocol (Week 4): [I Like / I Wonder / What If]
- Public product rubric (see below):
- Individual reflection journal: 

RUBRIC DIMENSIONS:
| Criterion | Exemplary (4) | Proficient (3) | Developing (2) | Beginning (1) |
|-----------|--------------|---------------|---------------|--------------|
| Content accuracy | | | | |
| Product quality | | | | |
| Collaboration | | | | |
| Communication | | | | |
| Reflection depth | | | | |

───────────────────────────────────────────
RESOURCES & MATERIALS
- 
- 

───────────────────────────────────────────
DIFFERENTIATION
- Support:
- Extension:
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

## Template E — 5E Science Lesson (Single or Multi-Day)

Best for: K-12 and introductory university science, STEM, and inquiry units.

```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
5E LESSON PLAN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Topic:
Subject:
Grade / Level:
Duration:
Essential Question:

───────────────────────────────────────────
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
Students will be able to:
1. 
2.

───────────────────────────────────────────
5E SEQUENCE

[ENGAGE — 5–10 min]
Hook / Phenomenon:
Prior knowledge question:
Student misconception to surface (if known):

[EXPLORE — 15–25 min]
Activity / Investigation:
Materials needed:
Student task (what they do):
Data/observation record format:
Teacher role (facilitate, observe, do NOT explain yet):

[EXPLAIN — 10–15 min]
Formal vocabulary introduced:
Key concept delivery method: [lecture / video / reading]
"Anchor" back to exploration: "Remember what you observed when...?"
Check for understanding technique:

[ELABORATE — 10–15 min]
Extension application:
New scenario or problem:
Connection to real world:

[EVALUATE]
Formative: [during lesson]
Summative: [assessment name + due date]
Self-assessment prompt:

───────────────────────────────────────────
DIFFERENTIATION
- Support:
- Extension:
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```
